newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian spot natgas prices strong on injections.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices strong on injections.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices softened slightly on Wednesday but were still strong amid warmer weather as players kept buying to fill depleted storage facilities.
"That's the sole factor driving our market," said a Calgary-based trader. "The marginal market is not getting enough supply and the marginal market is storage."

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.74/1.79 per gigajoule range, down a couple of cents from Tuesday and last week. May prices were discussed at about the same level, against a two cent drop from Tuesday.
Gas for U.S. Midwest and Northeast export markets, however, was talked higher on Wednesday in line with a surge in NYMEX and U.S. cash prices, traders said.

Gas at Niagara for Thursday delivery was quoted in the low US$2.40s per million British thermal units, up about a dime on the day. Monchy, Saskatchewan gas into the Northern Border Pipeline system was discussed in the mid-US$160s.
Marketers said rumors about pipeline problems along the flooding Red River in the Northern United States and southern Manitoba were rampant, but no cuts in deliveries had been made by operators.

In the west, Sumas gas eased again by a couple cents into the mid US$1.20s amid the gas compressor outage on Northwest Pipeline which has removed about 130 million cubic feet per day of deliveries on the system.
A Vancouver-based trader said the curtailed volumes were backed up in British Columbia causing the lower prices.
